_why: THE MONITORS PAYLOAD, pinned from both ends (round 65). The panel had a payload test of its own and the DEVICE had none: its file records the consequence in its own words — 'the shape is the contract, nothing validates it, and a wrong guess looks like data'. A hand-written fixture described a transition as {ts_ms, ok, reason}, which is plausible and wrong (the real one is {at_ms, up, lasted_ms}), and a transition the parser cannot place in time is DROPPED — so the card rendered with no transitions and no error. This file is the same contract the session row has: `required_by_panel` is the list read off the panel's parser, and `agent/src/monitor.rs` asserts the device SENDS every one of them while the panel's test asserts it READS them. A rename on either side now fails a test instead of quietly emptying a card.
_shape: read off agent/src/monitor.rs (Probe, Transition, summary_of, snapshot) — not from memory

example_http._why: THE SAME TARGET WATCHED AS A WEB UI, where the two fields a TCP target leaves null are the whole point: a status code says the page answered, and `last_expect_ok` says whether it answered WITH the text — 'no answer' and 'the answer did not say it' are different facts, which is why `Probe` keeps them apart.
